messages:
sam: heads up — got a report from support: after using the quick workflow switcher some customers see other org dashboards for ~10s then it snaps back. reproducing locally now. :eyes:
maria: can you paste repro steps? which switcher flow, browser, auth method?
sam: steps: login as org-42 -> open dashboard A -> cmd+k -> switch to org-77 -> click dashboard list -> observed cards from org-42 show for ~5-12s then replaced. happens on chrome + firefox.
sam: grabbing network + console logs.
sam: console.log snapshot:
```
[UI] quick-switcher: selected org=org-77
[API] GET /api/console/dashboards?orgId=org-77 200 120ms
[Cache] sessionPrefetch returned cached key=session:org-42:dashboards
[UI] render 50 items (source=cached)
```
maria: sounds like prefetch cache key isn't scoping by active session id after switch. do we use affinity headers on prefetch?
chris: prefetch service currently keys by userId+workspaceTag but that tag can be stale during rapid switch — there's a race between the router setting X-Workspace and the prefetch call. not adding TTL right now.
patrick: telemetry shows spike at 1712349000-1712349800 for prefetch cache hits from multiple orgs. looks like cross-org reuse.
alice: who rolled prefetch change last? any canary?
deploy-bot: deploy:prefetch-service v2.8.1 promoted to prod by @devops at 2024-04-11T15:12:07Z (canary 10%)
maria: ok, root cause hypothesis: quick-switch triggers client to change workspace header then fires prefetch RPC before session middleware updates server-side session mapping. prefetch uses cached session key (old workspace) -> returns old dashboards -> UI renders until explicit API returns.
chris: options:
- patch prefetch to include explicit X-Workspace header in request and *validate* against session mapping
- change cache key to include request-scoped nonce that the client flips on switch
- introduce short invalidation on switch event in frontend
which is least risky?
sam: quick frontend invalidation is fastest to rollback but feels brittle. stronger server-side validation safer.
patrick: server-side validation means adding validation lookup per prefetch call — perf hit. but we can make it a cheap check: compare incoming X-Workspace to cacheKey.workspace and if mismatch, bypass cache. micro-ops.
alice: I vote for server-side short-term: bypass cache when header mismatch, then add client nonce later. canary that change.
maria: agree. also add telemetry metric for "prefetch_cache_bypass_reason=workspace_mismatch" so we can measure.
chris: will open PR for prefetch-service: add header validation + metric. tag me for perf review.
chris: PR plan: add middleware that extracts X-Workspace from headers, compare to parsed cacheKey, if mismatch increment metric and skip cache, else proceed. minimal path.
sam: can we also add a UI safeguard — show skeleton placeholder until confirmed API returns, to avoid flashing wrong cards? UX plz?
alice: @sam can file a tiny frontend PR to show neutral skeleton on switch. UX ok with that.
patrick: I'll create incident/ticket: CONSOLE-5122 with priority P2, assign chris + sam, target hotfix tomorrow morning.
deploy-bot: incident created CONSOLE-5122 by patrick.
console-monitor-bot: alert: prefetch_cache_hit_ratio dropped by 18% at 2024-04-11T15:20:00Z (likely bypasses).
sam: thanks all. i'll attach logs from a customer session to the ticket.
maria: postmortem checklist: list of customers hit, timeline, canary window, and follow-up to add nonce-based key in 2 weeks.
chris: starting the server-side patch now, will request canary deploy 5% then ramp.
alice: I'll coordinate with support messaging.
sam: resolving for now but keeping thread open for rollout updates.
